Redirect-chain limit lowered from 10000 to 1000, so deep span trees are no longer joined
The loop that follows the redirect chain was changed from `for i = 0, 10000` to `for i = 0, 1000`. The removed comment said this limit means trees deeper than the limit may not be joined correctly. With a chain longer than 1000 hops, the loop exits before it reaches the real set root. The span is then attached to an intermediate set_span_id, and the segment is split across several sets. The change cuts the limit tenfold with no stated reason.

zunionstore default SUM aggregate distorts scores used by zpopmin eviction
`zunionstore set_key 2 set_key span_key` uses the default AGGREGATE SUM. When the same payload is present in both sets, for example after a redelivered span, its score (end_timestamp_precise) is added to itself. The later `zpopmin` evicts the lowest scores, so it then treats that span as much later than it really is and keeps it over genuinely later spans.
When a segment exceeds 1000 spans, the wrong spans can be evicted. Duplicated spans are favored over legitimate later ones.

comment_verdicts.text:
Pre-existing attendees can be sent the "new booking" email because the caller passes unfiltered guests as newGuests
sendAddGuestsEmails decides per attendee whether to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (new guest) or AttendeeAddGuestsEmail by checking newGuests.includes(attendee.email). The only caller, addGuests.handler.ts:168, passes the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests`, which has existing attendees and blacklisted addresses removed (lines 74-78). If the input includes an email that is already an attendee, as long as at least one other guest is new, that existing attendee matches newGuests.

Notification emails sent to the unfiltered guest list instead of the guests actually added
The handler filters the input into `uniqueGuests`. That removes guests who are already attendees and guests on BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Only `uniqueGuests` are persisted. But `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw `guests` input. A blacklisted address, or an existing attendee, therefore still gets an "added to booking" email even though it was rejected and not stored. The blacklist check also compares the un-lowercased `guest` against lowercased blacklist entries (line 77), so `Bad@x.

No upper bound on the number of guests per request
`guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`. The handler runs `createMany`, does a translation lookup per attendee and sends emails per guest, so the work grows with the array length. An authenticated attendee can submit very large arrays.
A single request can trigger a large number of attendee inserts and outbound emails, which is a resource-abuse and spam vector.

judge_pairs.reason: Email sender called with raw guests, so existing attendees treated as new and get wrong email.
sendAddGuestsEmails receives unfiltered guests, so existing attendees get added-to-booking emails.
Blacklist compares un-lowercased guest against lowercased entries, bypassing via mixed case.
Blacklist lowercased but guest compared as-is, so mixed-case addresses bypass filter.
Input not de-duplicated server-side, so repeated addresses create duplicate attendee rows.

comment_verdicts.text:
Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is cancelled when the request returns
The legacy write in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection now runs in a goroutine. Each goroutine calls context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) on the request-scoped ctx. In an apiserver that ctx is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, and the handler returns right after the method returns. The goroutine then usually calls Legacy.* with an already-cancelled context. The 10s timeout therefore never gets to apply. The goroutines also read the caller's obj, objInfo and options afte

Storage failures in Create and Update are recorded as legacy durations
When Storage.Create or Storage.Update fails (line 45 in Create, line 129 in Update), the code calls recordLegacyDuration(true, ...). The failure came from the unified storage, so it should call recordStorageDuration.
Storage errors are reported under the legacy metric. Dashboards and alerts show wrong data.

Delete uses the object name as the metric kind label and drops request-scoped log values
On success, Delete calls recordStorageDuration with `name` where every other call passes options.Kind. Delete also builds ctx with d.Log instead of the enriched `log`.
The kind label gets an unbounded set of values, one per deleted object name, which inflates metric cardinality. Downstream logs also lose the name, kind and method values.

DeleteCollection records the legacy duration as a storage metric
The legacy goroutine in DeleteCollection calls recordStorageDuration with the legacy error and start time. It should call recordLegacyDuration.
Storage metrics are polluted with legacy timings and errors. Legacy delete-collection metrics are never emitted.

judge_pairs.reason: Storage failure in Create/Update wrongly recorded via recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.
Delete passes name instead of options.Kind to metrics recording.
Delete builds ctx with d.Log instead of enriched log variable, losing name/kind/method values.
